finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST /hooks/test handler sends a server-side POST to a URL taken directly from the request body. The `pub` router has no auth middleware. The response status is returned to the caller, so it works as an oracle for internal hosts and ports. Cloud metadata endpoints and internal services are reachable.
finding.source: req.body.callback (JSON or form body of POST /hooks/test, supplied by any remote client)

trace.note: Route registered on the public router `pub`, with no requireAdmin or other auth
req.body.callback passed unmodified as the URL to axios.post
Upstream response status is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no DNS-rebinding protection. requireAdmin is applied only to `admin` (line 12), not `pub`. axios follows redirects by default, so a redirect can also bypass a naive check. No upstream middleware is visible, since only routes.js exists in the repo.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 registers POST /hooks/test on the `pub` router, which has no auth (requireAdmin is only applied to `admin` at line 12), and passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post at line 20 and returns the status at line 21; the only file in the repo is routes.js, so no upstream middleware is visible, but nothing in it validates the URL.

finding.claim: SSRF in the admin diagnostics fetch endpoint: a fully attacker-chosen URL is fetched server-side and the status is returned. Access is limited to admin sessions, so this is lower severity. It becomes exploitable through a compromised or malicious admin account, or through session or CSRF issues. A GET request carrying the admin session cookie could also trigger it.
finding.source: req.query.url (query string of GET /diagnostics/fetch, supplied by an admin user)

trace.note: Response status returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (lines 7-10) restricts access to admin sessions. There is no URL validation, allowlist, private-IP blocking, or redirect restriction. No CSRF protection is visible for this GET route.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) is an authorization check only; no URL validation exists.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12, 15, 16), but the sink at routes.js:15 is reachable only through admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which returns 403 for non-admin sessions at routes.js:8, so no unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker controls req.query.url, and the CSRF or session-compromise path is speculative and not shown in the code.
